text: Quick question for Dan Mlelen.
>> All right, let's see it.
>> Uh, why do we never hear about Asher
potentially being the mother of Yahweh
or Adonai as you would usually put it?
Um, the evidence seems to line up better
with that than her as a consort and yet
I never see it. Have I like missed
something? Was there some great big
debate that I'm not privy to? What's
happening there? Cheers.
Hey, thank you for a wonderful question.
I think most critical scholars of early
Israelite religion would suggest there
was a rather brief time period during
which Ashra would have been considered
the mother of Adonai. And this period
would have stretched from Adonai's
introduction to the pantheon on the
second tier all the way to the
conflation of Adoni and L. And that time
period was likely only around a century
or so. Adonai was probably conflated
with L or began to be conflated with L
rather soon after being introduced into
the pantheon. And once Adonai is
conflated with L, L's consort partner
wife, Asher becomes Adonai's consort
partner wife. And so in Deuteronomy 32:8
and9, this is I think the clearest
evidence we have for this early period
in the history of Adonai's presence in
the pantheon where they seem to be
represented as one of the Ben Elohim, as
one of the children of the most high god
Elon. And that would be the period where
Adonai would have been one of the
offspring of Asher and L. However,
again, Adonai would have been conflated
with L probably pretty quickly after
that. I suggest somewhere around 1,000
BCE. Maybe it took a couple centuries
for that understanding of Adonai's
identity to become the consensus view to
reach a critical mass. We can't really
say for sure. So while I think most
scholars who reconstruct a history of
Adonai similar to the way I and other
critical scholars do would suggest there
is a period where Adonai would have been
the son of Ashra. We don't really have
any texts or iconography or anything
that witness to that perspective on
their relationship. It's really the
postconlation relationship where Asher
and Adoni are partners that we have
reflected in inscriptions in iconography
and things like that. And then the later
representation of Asher as the queen of
heaven or as this divine image that is
associated with Adonai in the temple.
That's all reflective of the
postconlation
view of Adonai and Asher as partners. So
hopefully that explains how scholars
reconstruct that and why we don't really
hear many scholars talking about Asher
as the mother of Adonai and far more
commonly as the consort partner or wife
of Adonai. And the fit for this video
has been the death of Superman.
